first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates onboarding simplification improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. A guarded experiment is preferable to promotional pricing because pricing previously reduced 30-day retention, which conflicts with the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Verify the two most directly relevant archived records before committing and monitor retention and qualified conversion alongside completion and activation.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying the self-serve onboarding flow. This directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and the 6% activation decline. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%; SMB signup simplification also improved activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. Evaluate qualified revenue and retention as guardrails, since the SMB signup result had a 1% retention decline and does not establish effects outside SMB.

final2.rationale: Pivot the single experiment to a narrowly targeted, time-bounded promotional-price retention offer for demonstrably price-sensitive SMB accounts at churn risk. The competitor's deeper SMB price cut and doubled churn conversations create an immediate segment-specific threat, while inherited evidence supports pricing effectiveness for this segment. Do not broaden the offer: prior evidence found a material 30-day retention reduction, so measure incremental qualified revenue, post-promotion retention, downgrade behavior, and margin against a holdout before any expansion.
